details.description: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B is an 8-billion-parameter dense reasoning model that DeepSeek created by fine-tuning Meta's Llama-3.1-8B on roughly 800,000 reasoning traces generated by the full DeepSeek-R1 model, released in January 2025 alongside DeepSeek-R1. It carries R1's step-by-step 'thinking' style of reasoning for math, coding and logic tasks into a much smaller footprint. Fireworks AI serves it with a 131,000-token context length. It is released under the MIT license, layered on Meta's Llama 3.1 license for the underlying weights.
advantages: Scores 50.4% pass@1 on AIME 2024, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 89.1% pass@1 on MATH-500, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 49.0% pass@1 on GPQA Diamond, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 39.6% pass@1 on LiveCodeBench, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
disadvantages: DeepSeek's model card recommends capping output around 32,768 tokens and notes the model can 'bypass thinking pattern' on some queries, which may reduce answer quality.
Scores well below the larger 70B and 14B checkpoints in the same distilled family on every benchmark DeepSeek reports for this family.

DeepSeek's own API changelog labels this reasoning generation 'legacy R1' and discontinued the deepseek-reasoner model id in favor of the DeepSeek-V4 series by July 2026, though the open weights stay available on Hugging Face and via third-party hosts such as Fireworks AI.
use_cases: Multi-step reasoning and logic tasks on limited hardware
General text generation with an explicit chain-of-thought 'thinking' step

notes: DeepSeek's model card recommends a maximum generation length of 32,768 tokens for reliable output, well below the 131,072-token max_input/max_output in the catalog facts and the 131,000-token context Fireworks advertises; the catalog's larger figures are kept as authoritative per instructions, but users should know the maker's own tested/recommended length is much shorter. The model card gives no exact release day for this checkpoint, and Hugging Face's repo metadata shows it was published 2025-01-20, so the description was softened to 'January 2025' rather than the earlier '22 January'. DeepSeek's own API changelog (api-docs.deepseek.com/updates) shows deepseek-reasoner moved on from DeepSeek-R1 to DeepSeek-V3.1/V3.2-Exp in 2025 and then to the V4 series by mid-2026, referring to this generation as 'legacy R1'.
